context:
A monorepo package `@acme/format-kit` currently publishes all source files. Downstream packages import both the public entrypoint and deep internals:

```ts
import { formatCurrency } from '@acme/format-kit'
import { normalizeLocale } from '@acme/format-kit/src/locale'
import { parseMoney } from '@acme/format-kit/src/money/parse'
```

The package owner wants to add an `exports` map before the next minor release to reduce accidental public API surface. The current package metadata is:

```json
{
  "name": "@acme/format-kit",
  "version": "1.8.0",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "./dist/index.js",
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
  "files": ["dist", "src"],
  "scripts": {
    "prepack": "bun run build",
    "build": "tsc -p tsconfig.json"
  }
}
```

There are 11 internal workspace consumers of `src/locale`, 3 external customers known to use `src/money/parse`, and no documented API for deep imports. Support wants to avoid breaking paying customers without warning. Engineering wants to stop new deep imports immediately. The package README owns public API documentation. The repo convention is that TS/JS relative module specifiers are extensionless in source, but concrete paths in docs and package metadata keep real suffixes. Bun publish rewrites workspace protocols, so that is not a blocker by itself.
task: Plan the safest migration from deep imports to a public export map. Identify the boundary decision, sequencing, compatibility risks, and verification.
title: Package Export Map Migration Plan
